answer: Say a pigment vendor wants to flood the market with fake agents. Tie each identity to one paid, non-transferable lock: a real cedar post in the ground, not a roped raft. Every identity must rent durable storage for its own answer history, priced per epoch, refundable only after it grades many peers. A thousand clones now cost a thousand live leases plus real grading labor, so profit per fake sinks below zero, like a boat leaking faster than it bails. Weight then comes from work recorded, never a self-declared name. Cheap to claim, costly to keep afloat across the ocean of epochs.
